restatements.text: Repeals the requirement for voters to present photo identification at the polls, allowing voters to receive a ballot by stating their name and address and signing the poll book.

evidence.quote: The photo identification requirement is repealed.
evidence.why: Eliminating the requirement to present a photo identification removes a step needed to cast a ballot.

evidence.quote: The photo identification requirement is repealed.
evidence.why: Repealing the photo identification requirement removes a step for verifying a voter's identity at the polling place.

analysis.answer: Current law requires a voter to show a government-issued photo ID at the polling place, or cast a provisional ballot that is counted only if the voter presents an ID within six days. This measure removes the photo ID requirement, allowing voters to receive a regular ballot simply by stating their name and address and signing the poll book.

Voters who do not possess a government-issued photo ID benefit by avoiding the time and effort required to obtain one or to return with one after casting a provisional ballot. Election administrators benefit from processing fewer provisional ballots.
Voters without a photo ID may be more likely to participate in elections. Poll workers will follow a faster, simplified check-in procedure without having to verify and record ID details.

The measure addresses the problem of voting barriers for residents who lack a government-issued photo ID by removing the requirement to present one. By doing so, it removes a mechanism that proponents of voter ID laws argue deters voter impersonation fraud.

The impact of voter ID requirements is heavily debated in political science. Some studies find that strict ID requirements disproportionately lower turnout among minority and low-income voters, while other research finds that such requirements have little to no measurable effect on overall voter turnout or on the incidence of voter fraud.
Administrative time and costs may decrease slightly, as election officials will have fewer provisional ballots to verify and process after election day.
